key_insight: A lightweight step-attention decoder can better adapt DINOv3 features for anterior eye segmentation than standard convolutional or transformer baselines.
clinical_relevance: This could improve robustness of anterior eye segmentation across varied clinical imaging protocols, supporting more reliable ocular biometrics and downstream image analysis.
method: Built on a distilled DINOv3 ViT-Small backbone.
Adds step-attention feature refinement to progressively adapt multi-level transformer features.
Uses a lightweight convolutional decoder for efficient dense prediction.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on 333 clinically acquired anterior eye images across eight protocols and seven anatomical classes, and achieved 85.55% mIoU when fully fine-tuned with strong generalization to four unseen public datasets.
watch_item: Performance was shown in retrospective datasets, so real-world deployment still needs validation across sites, devices, and annotation workflows.
paper_title: Step-Attention Refinement of DINOv3 Features for Efficient Anterior Eye Segmentation
